Can you explain the main options in simple terms?

Absolutely! Here’s a simple breakdown of the main options you’ll find at Heirloom:

Roses: Our specialty! We offer many varieties of own-root roses, which are grown in containers and shipped with soil. You can browse by type (like climbers or shrubs), color, fragrance, or what grows best in your area.

Perennials: These are plants that come back year after year, such as lavender, hydrangea, and hosta. They add lasting beauty to your garden and are shipped in containers.

Bulbs: These include flowers like tulips, daffodils, and allium. Bulbs are usually planted in the fall and bloom in spring. We also offer pre-potted tulips and daffodils in spring.

Soil Amendments & Fertilizers: Products like compost, worm castings, and fertilizers help your plants grow strong and healthy.

Garden Markers: Metal tags or stakes you can use to label your plants.

You can explore these by using the menu at the top of our website. If you want help picking the right plant for your space, let me know your location or what you’re looking for, and I’ll help you narrow it down!

turns.replyText:
How do I use it properly the very first time?

Here’s a simple guide for using the Get Growing Bundle the very first time:

If you’re planting in the ground:

Dig a hole for your rose.
Add about 3 inches of soil to the bottom of the hole.
Mix in the 100% Natural Aged Cow Manure and about 1 cup of Heirloom's Bone Meal with the soil at the bottom.
Place your rose in the hole.
Fill the rest of the hole with soil and the Mint Compost (one 1.5 quart bag per plant, mixed into the topsoil or used as a top dressing).
Water thoroughly.
Mix 4 oz of Founders Fish Fertilizer per gallon of water and use it to water your rose at planting. Repeat every 4–6 weeks.

If you’re planting in a container:

Mix the Cow Manure and Bone Meal into your potting soil before planting.
Place your rose in the container and fill with the soil mixture.
Use Mint Compost as a top dressing around the base.
Water thoroughly.
Use Founders Fish Fertilizer (4 oz per gallon of water) at planting, then every 3–4 weeks.

These steps will give your rose a healthy start! If you need more detailed planting tips, just ask.
